<description>
**Problem:** Kernel applications can only override the time validation uses for the whole process, with `btck_set_mock_time` (#35496). Every chainstate manager in the process sees the same time, so a time set for one test, run, or thread leaks into the others unless the application remembers to reset it.

**Solution:** Add `btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_clock_time` and `btck_chainstate_manager_set_clock_time`, which set the time for a single chainstate manager, before it is created (so it also applies to checks made while it loads the chainstate) and afterwards. Validation code gets the time from a new `ChainstateManager::Now()` method instead of calling `NodeClock::now()` directly. Details are in the commit messages.

Keeping the time in the chainstate manager instead of in a global makes kernel applications more reliable, because state from one run or thread can't affect another.

Other commits:

- The first commit fixes a rare timing race in the `chainstatemanager_ibd_exit_after_loading_blocks` test, where test code and validation code read the clock separately and assumed they got the same time.
- The last two commits switch that test and the `utxo_total_supply` fuzz target to the new per-chainman clock, as suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35557#issuecomment-4763429282.

Two related commits that were previously part of this PR are in a follow-up branch based on it, https://github.com/ryanofsky/bitcoin/commits/pr/kclock2: a mempool refactor to represent clock times consistently, and a change that makes `NodeClock::now()` unavailable in libbitcoinkernel so kernel code can't use the system clock by accident.
</description>

Thanks, that's fair, and the PR was trying to do too much. I made it smaller: it now has the test race fix, the `btck_chainstate_manager_set_clock_time` API (now with an options setter too, see [the separate comment about construction time](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35557#discussion_r4498695811)), and the two tests using the new clock (`chainstatemanager_ibd_exit_after_loading_blocks` and the `utxo_total_supply` fuzz target you suggested). The mempool time point refactor and the commit making `NodeClock::now()` a link error in kernel code are now in a follow-up branch based on this one: https://github.com/ryanofsky/bitcoin/commits/pr/kclock2. I know you suggested keeping this in one piece, so I can open the follow-up as a PR whenever that would help review.

On maflcko's question in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35557#issuecomment-5313546704: I think this is still relevant. #35496 sets the time for the whole process, and this sets it for one chainstate manager, so a time set for one test, run, or thread can't leak into another.

One argument for your callback idea that I missed before: stringintech pointed out in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35496#issuecomment-5207535775 that a long call like `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` may need to read the time several times, for example when the IBD status is re-checked after each connected block. A fixed time set beforehand can't advance during the call, and a callback can. My prototype in 3d513c5d03ceb8d33dc8e19c07149e3337c64ac6 only made the time a shared settable value, so it didn't really test your suggestion. I still think a setter is simpler to start with, since a fixed time is what deterministic tests and replays want, but I'm happy to switch to a callback if you or others think it's worth the extra API surface.

Looking again, there is one already: `btck_chainstate_manager_create` loads the chainstate, which runs this future-tip check and can latch the IBD status off, before the caller can call `btck_chainstate_manager_set_clock_time`. So I added `btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_clock_time`, which sets the time before the chainstate manager is created, and kept `btck_chainstate_manager_set_clock_time` for changing it afterwards, so the time can still be moved any number of times, as you preferred.
